newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares end weak, further decline seen.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares end weak, further decline seen.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 2.1 percent on Monday and traders forecast the market could continue its slide for months if foreign investors fail to return to the Slovenian market.

"If international investors decide to stay away due to extra costs or fear of further unexpected central bank decrees the market could fall at least for the next six months because domestic investors do not have the capital to sustain its current capitalisation," one broker said.

The Bank of Slovenia five weeks ago blocked foreign investment by saying international investors would have to open custodian accounts at Slovenian banks in order to trade in Slovenian securities. Since then the blue-chip index fell by 17.7 percent.
The banks said they would open first custodian accounts at the end of March. They said the cost would be 12 percent of the amount handled.
"The bourse market is almost dead due poor liquidity that may continue until international investors return," said Toni Apollonio, an analyst of bank A banka.
The 11-share SBI index fell 29.17 points to 1,361.82.
Bank SKB was most actively traded, down 2.45 percent to 53,700 tolars on volume of 1,542 shares.
Overall nine shares fell, three rose, four were unchanged and 10 were untraded.
Turnover rose to 126.7 million tolars from 54 million on Friday but traders said the rise was insignificant because it was made in a small number of transactions.
Bank Probanka was the leading decliner, down 9.98 percent to 21,100 tolars on volume of 19 shares.
Financial consultancy Primofin was the top gainer, up 7.51 percent to 15,900 on volume of 83 shares.
